name: Breast health clinics
summary: How expats find breast specialists in Singapore for lumps, screening mammograms, biopsy coordination, and post-cancer surveillance — including how breast clinics relate to gynae and oncology pathways.
body:
Breast concerns are high-anxiety and time-sensitive. Singapore offers one-stop breast clinics (imaging + surgeon consult), public hospital breast units, and private specialists. Expats may also arrive mid-surveillance after overseas treatment and need continuity.

## What these clinics cover
- Symptomatic lumps, nipple discharge, mastitis
- Screening mammography / ultrasound pathways by age and density
- Biopsy (core, vacuum-assisted) and pathology follow-up
- Benign disease surveillance vs excision decisions
- Coordination into oncology and reconstructive surgery when malignant

Obstetrics-gynaecology is not a substitute for dedicated breast assessment when imaging is abnormal — use the right specialty early.

## Screening and cost
Employer screens and “executive health” packages vary in quality. Prefer centres that can recall you for additional views and biopsy without restarting at a new brand. Check whether your insurance treats screening as wellness (often excluded) vs diagnostic imaging after symptoms (more often claimable).

## How to choose
Look for radiologist + surgeon collaboration, clear timelines from abnormal image to biopsy result, and nurse navigators for cancer pathways. For breastfeeding-related issues, confirm lactation-aware protocols. Bring prior mammogram disks — density comparison matters.

## Practical tip
Book symptomatic slots rather than waiting for an annual package if you feel a new lump. Same-week private imaging is often available; public pathways are solid but referral-gated. Take a support person to result discussions when cancer is on the differential.
